items.title: 52145_Andrew Blakeney oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee does not speak in the provided context; the mention of Jack McVea is made by the Interviewer.

ctx.x: Well you know Mr. Satchel McVea was indeed a legend. He was the father of Jack McVea and he started many musicians in Los Angeles playing; he played for many of the social affairs of the white community at that time. He was the father of Jack McVea and he was one of the black musicians that refused to join the union. He had quite a bit of work at that time without being a member of the musicians union, so he sort of rebelled and I don't think during his whole career he was ever a member of either Local 767 which…
"colored union," or later Local 47. [He was] quite an important man in early musical history of Los Angeles.
